lesson.subtitle: Lesson 4 -- A Day in My Life
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Carlos Henrique Rodrigues | Lesson 4 -- A Day in My Life
lesson.grammar_point: present simple with he and she (he works, he does not work, Does he...?)

listenings.text: My father is seventy years old, and he has a very organized day. He gets up at six. He walks in the park for thirty minutes, and then he has breakfast with my mother. He works in the morning, but only in the morning. He has lunch at home. In the afternoon, he reads the news and he calls his friends. He doesn't work on Saturdays. On Saturdays, he cooks for the family.

I have a family company. We sell furniture. For thirty years, I did everything. Now my son runs the company. He gets up very early, he answers all the emails, and he talks to the team. I go to the office three days a week. I have meetings with the bank, and I help with the big customers. My son doesn't need me every day, and that is good. He knows the business.

extra_audio.text: Carlos gets up at eight. He has coffee and answers messages. At nine thirty, he goes to the office. He has a meeting with the bank. At three, he goes home. In the evening, he watches a good movie.

paras: Carlos is sixty-five. He is an accountant and an economist, and he runs two family companies: a car rental company and a company that makes cars bulletproof. He gets up at eight. He has coffee, and he answers messages on his phone. He likes the phone more than the apps.

At nine thirty, he goes to the office. Every day he visits company A or company B. He has a meeting with the bank, or with a customer, or with his son. His son works with him, and now his son runs the companies. Carlos does not work late. At three, he goes home.

In the evening, he has dinner and he calls people on the phone again. He does not read many books, but he watches a good movie before bed. And on Tuesdays and Thursdays, at four in the afternoon, he has an English class.
